title: What is Flexbox?
body:
Flexbox is a powerful one-dimensional layout module in CSS. It provides an efficient way to distribute space among items in a container, even when their size is unknown or dynamic. 

It simplifies the creation of responsive and adaptable user interfaces, enabling easier alignment and distribution of elements.

title: Summary
bullets: Flexbox is designed for one-dimensional layouts.
Flex items are direct children of the flex container.

title: Flex Direction
body:
The `flex-direction` property specifies the direction of the flex items in the flex container. It can be set to `row` (default), `row-reverse`, `column`, or `column-reverse`. 

This property determines the main axis, which is used for aligning and distributing space among the items. Understanding this is vital for layout control.

title: Row and Column

title: Flex Wrap
body:
The `flex-wrap` property controls whether flex items should wrap onto multiple lines if they exceed the container's width. It can be set to `nowrap` (default), `wrap`, or `wrap-reverse`. 

This is essential for creating responsive layouts that adapt to different screen sizes, preventing overflow and ensuring content remains visible.

title: Summary
bullets: `flex-wrap` manages line breaks for overflowing items.
These properties are fundamental to Flexbox layout.

title: Justify Content
body:
The `justify-content` property defines how flex items are distributed along the main axis. Common values include `flex-start` (default), `flex-end`, `center`, `space-between`, and `space-around`. 

It allows for precise control over the horizontal or vertical alignment of items within the flex container, creating visually appealing layouts.

title: Justify Content Examples
description: This code snippet demonstrates how to use `justify-content` to center flex items.

title: Align Items
body:
The `align-items` property defines how flex items are aligned along the cross axis. Values include `stretch` (default), `flex-start`, `flex-end`, `center`, and `baseline`. 

This property is crucial for vertical alignment within a flex container, ensuring items are positioned correctly relative to each other and the container's edges.

description: This code snippet demonstrates how to use `align-items` to center flex items vertically.

title: Summary
bullets: `justify-content` aligns items on the main axis.
`align-items` aligns items on the cross axis.
Mastering these properties unlocks powerful layout control.
